back: How many times larger the image is than the real object: image size ÷ actual size (no units, written ×400).
The ability to distinguish two points close together as separate points; the smaller the distance resolved, the more detail visible.

front: Actual size from image size and magnification?
back: Actual size = image size ÷ magnification (both lengths in the same unit).

front: Approximate resolution of a light microscope and of a TEM?
back: Light microscope about 200 nm; TEM about 0.5 nm (textbook values vary).
notes: Set by the wavelength of the radiation: light 400–700 nm, electrons far shorter.

front: Why does an electron microscope have higher resolution than a light microscope?
back: Electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light, so points much closer together can be distinguished.

front: TEM or SEM: which gives a 3D surface view?
back: SEM: electrons scanned over a metal-coated surface. The TEM passes electrons through a thin section and shows internal detail in 2D.

front: Value of one eyepiece graticule division?
back: (Number of stage divisions × length of one stage division) ÷ number of eyepiece divisions; recalibrate for each objective.
A structure or feature seen in a preparation that was not present in the living cell, caused by fixing, staining or sectioning.
